This fixes a pre-existing dynamic-array bug on the generic style-write path, unrelated to the decimal round trip; it is not listed in the task's Tasks/Known-deviations and the spill-metadata persistence invariant it establishes is not recorded in docs/design/sheets/calculator.md (which is where spill metadata is documented) or sheet-style.md.

samples.summary: Scope creep in `format.ts`: the triple-fallback `safeFormat` (bad locale → bad options → bare number), the `clampDecimals` guard inside `formatValue`, and `currencyDecimals`' Intl round-trip go beyond what the round-trip issue needs (a clamp in `changeDecimals`/`getActiveDecimalState` would bound the buttons). It is hostile/imported-`dp` hardening bundled into a UX-reversibility change; it is at least documented in the design doc, but it widens the blast radius of this PR to every render path.
samples.evidence: formatValue now clamps every dp it is handed; safeFormat gains two extra fallbacks; new hostile-input test block in format.test.ts.

samples.summary: Approach/scale fit: for `column`/`row`/`all` selections the new decimal path walks every populated cell in the selection up to three times per button press (`selectionRendersAt`, `unsetKeepsRendering`, then `unsetRangeStyleValues`' cell scan). sheet-style.md's documented `setRangeStyle` design is explicitly the opposite — "For column/row/all selections, stores styles at the column/row/sheet level instead of iterating every cell" — and the doc's Consequences list does not mention that the decimal buttons now break that property for whole-sheet selections.
samples.evidence: selectAllCells sets ranges to the full dimensionRange (sheet.ts:3015); each helper calls this.store.getGrid(range) over it.

samples.summary: `defaultKeys` pinning materializes an inherited value onto individual cells (`collectStyleValuesToPin` → `setStyle`), permanently detaching those cells from the column/row/sheet layer they inherited `nf` from: a later column-level format change will no longer reach them. The design doc records that pinning happens but not this inheritance-detachment consequence. It also adds a general-purpose `options.defaultKeys` parameter to `setRangeStyle` with exactly one caller, which is a broader abstraction than the issue asks for.
samples.evidence: sheet.ts:3792-3804 writes the pinned inherited value as an explicit cell style after the range patch lands; test 'should keep a neighbour format inherited from a column style' relies on it.

samples.summary: The `setRangeStyle(style)` section of the design doc was not updated with the new `options.defaultKeys` parameter — its semantics are described only inside the "Increase / decrease decimal places" section, so a reader of the write-semantics section sees a signature that no longer matches.
samples.evidence: Doc diff adds an `unsetRangeStyleValues` section and decimal rules, but the setRangeStyle bullets above are unchanged while the method gained a second argument.

samples.summary: `getActiveDecimalPlaces` is touched (clamped) but has no caller anywhere in the repo now that the view routes through `changeDecimals`; it duplicates a subset of `getActiveDecimalState`. Dead API worth removing rather than maintaining two decimal-state accessors.

finding.evidence: changeDecimals only unsets when `unsetKeepsRendering`; test 'should keep the grouping separators the step would flatten' asserts the `{dp:1, nf:'number'}` residue for '1234.5'.

verdict.reason: The claimed evidence checks out exactly. sheet.ts:4331-4349 gates the inheritance-restoring unset on unsetKeepsRendering(), and unsetKeepsRendering (sheet.ts:4414-4442) refuses whenever removing the keys would change formatValue output — which is precisely the grouped-value case, so '1234.5' and any user-chosen nf:'number' fall through to the explicit write at sheet.ts:4351-4362 and retain a {dp, nf:'number'} residue. The test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:94-112 asserts that residue after a -1/+1 round trip, and :114+ asserts it for a user-chosen number format. The narrowing is recorded rather than met: docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:214-233 explicitly calls it "a narrower guarantee than 'always'" with "exactly two situations" that keep a residue, and docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:3-18, :100-102 says it was "narrowed during review from the issue's absolute wording". No refutation ground applies: the code is present as described, reachable (a shipped, test-asserted behavior), and an unmet acceptance criterion is major under this lens. The decisive artifact — issue #845's acceptance table — is not present in the working tree, so I cannot verify whether it lists a grouped or formatted cell; the todo's reference to "the 12.5 row of the issue's table" hints the table may be ungrouped-only, but that is not proof. Confidence low because that ambiguity is exactly what the finding asks the verifier to settle and the repository does not contain the issue text.

finding.summary: Headline outcome ("Increase then Decrease leaves the cell exactly as it started") is knowingly not met for grouped values and user-chosen `nf: 'number'`
finding.evidence: The task doc's outcome is absolute: "Increase decimal places followed by Decrease decimal places must leave a cell exactly as it started — including leaving no dp/nf behind" (docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:3-5). The implementation's `unsetKeepsRendering` gate means any value ≥ 1000 (`1234.5`) keeps a `{dp, nf:'number'}` residue after an equal number of increases/decreases — asserted as intended by the new test 'should keep the grouping separators the step would flatten' (packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:96-113) and recorded as a 'Known deviation' in the todo (:87-89) and in sheet-style.md:262-266. The deviation is documented and argued for, but it is a partial fulfilment of the stated outcome rather than the outcome; a reviewer/verifier should confirm the deviation was accepted on the issue (#845) and not just self-granted in the task file.

verdict.reason: The substantive claim verifies against the repository. `Sheet.changeDecimals` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4315-4363) only restores inheritance when `unsetKeepsRendering` (sheet.ts:4414-4442) agrees, so a grouped value or a user-chosen `nf: 'number'` deliberately retains a `{dp, nf: 'number'}` residue after an equal number of increases/decreases. That residue is asserted as intended by the test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts:94-112 and by 'should keep a grouped number format the user chose' (:114-127). The repo's own docs concede the gap against the issue's wording: docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:229-231 ('Both are accepted deviations from the absolute wording of the issue') and :286-289, plus docs/tasks/active/20260818-sheets-decimal-round-trip-todo.md:11-18 and :91-102, and the lessons file :59-60. The reviewer's line citations are imprecise (todo:3-9 states the narrowed 'Outcome as shipped', not the absolute wording; 'Known deviations' begins at :91, not :87), but that is a citation slip, not a not-present refutation — the deviation itself is exactly as described. No guard removes it, and under the design-fit rubric a knowing partial fulfilment of the originating issue's outcome is in-lane and major by kind. Issue #845's own acceptance text does not exist anywhere in the working tree (grep for '845' returns only the task/lessons files), so I cannot establish that the narrowing was accepted on the issue rather than self-granted in the task file — which is the open question the finding raises. No named refutation ground applies.
